texts: give me a doha: people haggle over sandalwood in the market like it will make them rich forever
In the market's glitter the sandalwood is weighed and sold, yet what cannot be sold slips past unseen.
Write a doha about a merchant who spends his days selling sandalwood in the busy market, piling up coins, and never noticing that the wealth he holds is not truly his and never stays.
sandalwood, market, empty gain
My uncle sold sandalwood in the market for forty years, and when he retired he sat in an empty house wondering what all the deals had been for.
I want a doha about a moth rushing in excitement toward its own ruin and a potter's clay pots that look solid yet will crack, both teaching that what seems so attractive and permanent is not real.
hey a doha w/ a moth and a potter? like things look real but arent
moth, potter, false attraction
My brother quit his job to chase a get-rich scheme that looked perfect, and now he's broke. Our old potter neighbour just said moths never learn.
The moth is dazzled, the clay vessel proud, and neither sees how brief the show.
Please write a doha about how people run after wealth, status and comfort believing these will last forever, when in reality everything they cling to is passing and will slip away without warning.
need a doha on how nothing in this world is really ours
O restless mind that grasps what was never yours; open your hand, and see it was never held.
nothing here is permanent
I worked for twenty years to build up a big house and bank balance, and after the layoff I realized none of it was holding me up.
The fish rushes to the glittering lamp, and finds the dark waiting there.
My son stares at the bright lamp of his phone all night, hooked like a fish on whatever it shows him, convinced the next purchase will make him happy.
doha with a fish and a lamp about being fooled by shiny things
Compose a doha where a fish is lured by the glimmer of a lamp, thinking it is something good to chase, only to find that what attracted it was not real and led it astray.
fish, lamp, false glitter
potter's pots, passing things
The potter's vessel shines at the wheel, yet already the crack is sleeping inside it.
I would like a doha about a potter's pots that people admire and fight to buy, though every one of them is made of clay that will return to dust, just like everything else we think we own.
doha about pots made by a potter, nothing lasts but ppl still hold on
My grandmother's favourite clay pot, made by the potter down our lane, cracked this morning, and she wept as if she had lost a person.

Write a doha about a man who wears sandalwood paste on his forehead and counts his prayer beads loudly while his heart is stuck on property and profit, so the things meant to free him only decorate his attachment.
sandalwood, beads, attachment
Doha about someone with sandalwood and prayer beads but still obsessed w money
Sandalwood on the brow, beads in the hand, yet the heart is bound to gold.
My neighbour starts every day with a sandalwood tilak and his prayer beads, then spends the rest of it arguing over a few feet of land.
potter, beads, fleeting things
hey doha pls: prayer beads and a potter's clay, all gonna crumble anyway
My father makes clay pots at his wheel and also counts his prayer beads daily; lately he tells me everything we cling to will crumble like his pots.
Write a doha that places the potter's clay vessel next to a string of prayer beads, saying both are empty to the person who clings to them, because what seems solid and sacred is as passing as dust.
Beads in the hand and clay on the wheel, both will go; only the clinging remains.
Compose a doha about the moth that dives toward what seems bright and the fish that bites at what looks like food, both losing their lives to a thing that only appeared to be what they wanted.
I lost my savings last year to a scheme that looked too good, and my mother just said moth and fish are smarter than men.
Moth to the false brightness, fish to the hidden hook, and man to the glitter of gold.
moth, fish, false attraction
doha idea: moth and fish both get tricked by what looks good
O traveller, why clasp at what the next breath steals? The glitter is borrowed, and the lender is time.
doha about how everything in this world is an illusion
After my flat was repossessed I kept thinking, what exactly was all that hard work holding onto?
worldly attachment, loss
Please write a doha for someone who spent a lifetime collecting status, property and praise, and finally saw that none of it was real or truly his, only a show that held his attention for a while.
I'd like a doha about how the world looks solid and trustworthy, how we invest our hopes in people and possessions, and how it all turns out to be a passing show that fools us again and again.
I got promoted last month and felt like I'd finally arrived, but a week later I felt exactly as empty as before.
write a doha about how happiness from stuff doesn't last
false worldly pleasures
The world dresses itself in splendour and the foolish heart says, this is mine, forever.
In the market of the world the boat of life drifts, loaded with wares that the sea will take.
Write a doha about a merchant who loads his boat with goods from the market, hoping to grow rich, not seeing that the whole cargo and the voyage itself are passing things that cannot be kept.
My cousin sold off his land to buy a boat and start trading in the city market, convinced that wealth would finally make him secure.
doha pls about market and boat and how greed is blinding
market, boat, false wealth
Compose a doha for the person who keeps saying just a little more about money and success, never realizing that what they chase keeps moving away, and that the wanting itself is the trap.
He who chases every glitter loses the quiet that was already his.
endless wanting
Every time I buy something I wanted for months, I enjoy it for a day and then start wanting the next thing.
need a doha about greed and attachment lol
Compose a doha about a fish that follows a passing boat in hope of food, deceived by what looks like kindness and plenty, just as we follow the world's tempting promises to our own harm.
My friend took a job abroad on a fishing boat that promised big money, and he is back with nothing but debts.
fish, boat, tempting promises
The fish swims after the boat's shadow, hungry for a promise that was never given.
doha about a fish following a boat thinking its food, but its a trap
I want a doha about a moth that falls into a deep well while chasing something bright that seemed to be real, a story of how the glitter of the world leads the unwary into dark places.
The moth that follows the glitter leaves no trace but a ripple in the well's dark mouth.
doha w moth and a well about being fooled by looks
A guy at work lost everything following a flashy investor, and my grandfather said the moth always ends up in the well.
moth, well, deception
My uncle loves fishing and prayer beads in equal measure, but he will quarrel for hours over a tiny profit from his catch.
The fish is caught by a thread, the heart by a handful of coins; the beads count the days away.
Write a doha about a man who turns his prayer beads daily but whose mind is on the fish he will sell, showing how worldly profit keeps a heart tied even while the hands pretend to be free.
doha with fish and prayer beads about attachments
fish, prayer beads, attachment
My sister sacrificed her health for a corner office and just got laid off by email, and she's sitting in the dark asking what it was all for.
can I get a doha on losing everything you thought was yours
false security, loss

Please write a doha about the shock of discovering that the status, savings and relationships we leaned on were never as solid as we believed, and how the world keeps deceiving those who trust it too much.
The world smiles, and the sleeper believes; then morning comes, and the smile was empty.
doha about a well that looks full but is dry? like fake abundance
The well appears deep and brimming, yet the thirsty find only the echo of their own voice.
Write a doha about a person who trusts the well of worldly pleasures to quench every thirst, and keeps lowering his bucket again and again, only to find it never fills him.
well, empty promise
Our village well went dry this summer, and I kept returning to it anyway, hoping it would be full like before.
Compose a doha about a person who sails confidently in a boat full of holes, trusting its shiny paint, a picture of the way we trust a world that looks sturdy and is quietly sinking.
I put everything into a startup my friend swore was a sure thing, and now we're both stranded. It looked as sturdy as a brand new boat.
boat, false security
Beautiful is the boat, painted and proud, and the water already seeping through.
doha about a boat that looks fine but sinks, like worldly stuff

I'd like a doha about a man who keeps drawing from the well of worldly pleasures, believing each draught will satisfy him, though the thirst only grows, since the well was never meant to quench what he truly needs.
I keep reaching for the next promotion and the next vacation, and each time the satisfaction fades before the well of excitement even fills.
well, thirst, worldly pleasure
Deep goes the rope into the well of desire, and the bucket comes up with nothing but another thirst.
doha about a well that never satisfies, a metaphor for chasing wealth
false worldly pleasures
All that gleams in the world is borrowed, and soon enough it is called back.
My house was flooded and I lost most things, but the odd part is how little I miss them now that they are gone.
Write a doha about the way the world presents comfort, fame and pleasure as if they will last, until a single reversal shows how fragile and unreal all of it always was.
short doha on worldly attachments being meaningless
Compose a doha about a well that mirrors the sky so beautifully that people believe the reflection is real and reach for it, though it is just an appearance that vanishes with a ripple.
In the still well the moon seems close enough to hold; reach in, and it breaks.
I kept believing my ex would come back, like I could reach down into the well and bring the old days up again.
doha about a well, a reflection in the water, and not being real
well, reflection, falsehood
Write a doha about a potter proudly selling clay vessels perfumed with sandalwood, both of which seem valuable but come to dust in time, a lesson on how false the sense of permanence is.
doha: potter's pots and sandalwood, all will turn to dust
My grandfather the potter always perfumed his finest clay pieces with sandalwood and sold them at a premium, then laughed that it all breaks someday.
potter, sandalwood, fleeting
Fragrant the sandalwood, polished the clay, and both returning to dust as quietly as they came.

I'd like a doha to remind us that the things the world makes seem so valuable, like titles, houses and applause, are nothing but appearances that fade, and that attachment to them brings only pain in the end.
The world's fair promise delights the eyes, but behind it nothing waits.
doha about not getting attached to worldly things
I cried when my phone broke today, and then I realized it's just a phone and I'm acting like I lost a person.
clinging to things
Write a doha about a clay lamp made by a potter that burns brightly for a few hours then goes out, showing how the glow of pleasures in the world looks permanent but is brittle and brief.
On Diwali I bought a dozen clay lamps from the potter and arranged them neatly, and the next morning only soot and broken pieces were left.
potter, lamp, brief glow
doha: clay lamp from a potter, shines then goes out, like worldly stuff
Born of clay and fed with oil, the little lamp laughs at the night, till morning breaks it.
fish, well, deception

Compose a doha about a fish that thinks the well is the whole world and the small piece of sky above is everything, a picture of the way the mind trusts a narrow, passing world and never sees the truth.
I never left my little town and thought it was all there was, until a trip to the city showed me how small my well was, like a fish in it.
doha pls: fish in a well thinks thats the whole world
In the well, the fish speaks of the sea with all the confidence of one who has never left.
doha on how we waste our life chasing stuff
My dad worked every Sunday for thirty years to build a business, and now he's too ill to enjoy the money, and neither of us knows what it was for.
How the heart runs after a passing show, and weeps when it ends.
chasing the unreal

Write a doha about how human beings spend all their strength gathering things that will not last, deceived by appearances, and only at the end of life notice they've missed the one thing that was real.
The woodcutter hacks the sandalwood and counts his coins, unaware he has traded the sweetness for the sale.
Compose a doha about a seller who cuts and sells fragrant sandalwood for profit, caught up in dreams of becoming wealthy, forgetting that the worth lay in the fragrance and not in the trade.
My father inherited a sandalwood business and spent his whole life fighting relatives over it, and I wonder now what he had actually won.
doha with sandalwood about greed and attachment
sandalwood, greed
Write me a doha about how everything we love and cling to in this world, like our home, fame and family titles, fools us into thinking it is permanent, while it quietly slips from our hands each day.
When my grandmother's house was sold, I walked from room to room realizing I had treated every wall like it would stand forever.
doha, theme: the world isn't what it seems
The world glitters on the surface and hollows beneath; wise is he who sees both.
unreal world
The moth is drawn to ruin, the beads turn without end, and the heart that clings knows neither rest nor release.
Write a doha about a person who counts prayer beads in the morning and then flutters like a moth after profit and pleasure all day, not noticing how his own attachments are burning his peace.
My cousin does his morning prayers with his beads and then spends the rest of the day gambling on stocks, always restless like a moth, always sure the next win will fix it.
doha with a moth and prayer beads about greed
moth, beads, restless greed
prayer beads, worldly pull
My grandfather clutched his prayer beads and still kept asking about the land papers on every visit; he couldn't let go of what he had.
I'd like a doha about an old man who keeps turning prayer beads yet whose mind is tied to property and savings, showing how worldly attachment follows us even into our devotions.
doha: prayer beads in hand, but head full of money
The beads slip through the fingers, and the mind slips after gold.

Compose a doha about a large leafy tree that people assume will always be there, offering shade and fruit, until it falls in a storm, a reminder that what feels stable in the world can vanish in a day.
tree, shade, passing
doha: we think the tree will always be there but it wont
Proud the tree stands with its green crown, and the wind, laughing, already knows its name.
We played under the old tree of our house for my entire childhood, and when it was cut for the new road, it felt like a piece of the past was erased.
boat, potter, empty hope
My father makes clay pots at the potter's wheel and carries them by boat to sell in the next town, hoping the profit will finally make us secure.
Write a doha about a potter who loads his clay wares onto a boat to sell far away, hoping to become rich, not knowing that both the boat and the clay and the hope are all passing things.
The potter's wares sail on a boat of hope, and clay and hope and boat will each return to dust.
doha with a boat and a potter and wealth being an illusion
hey doha: a moth and prayer beads, being fooled by what looks holy
My aunt turns her prayer beads while watching her TV shows about jewellery, and last year she lost a lot of money chasing a shiny deal like a moth.
Moth to the bright, hand to the beads, and neither finds what each seeks.

Please compose a doha in which a restless moth and a worshipper with prayer beads are both drawn by desire, though one flies toward its ruin and the other counts away his life, both deceived by what seems to satisfy.
moth, prayer beads, desire
We planted a tree in our yard when my daughter was born, and now that she lives abroad I realize how fast everything we held dear has drifted away.

Write a doha about a tree that looks permanent to the person standing in its shade, who builds his plans under it, unaware that every season carries it and him toward the end, all part of a passing show.
doha pls about a tree n how nothing really lasts
tree, passing world
Green, the tree believes it is eternal, and the birds that nest in it believe it too.
doha about being fooled by appearances

I want a doha about how people are charmed by the shiny surface of life, spend everything on pleasures and possessions, and only find out later that all of it was a passing trick that left them empty.
I bought the biggest car I could afford to impress my coworkers, and the day I drove it home I felt absolutely nothing.
false happiness
The world sings sweetly to the sleeping heart, and the song ends when the heart awakes.
Passing is the feast and passing is the hunger; he who clings to either has lost the quiet between.
need a doha about letting go of worldly attachment
Please write a doha about how the more we cling to wealth, family pride and reputation, the more we suffer, because all of these are borrowed things the world will take back sooner than we expect.
I spent three hours arguing with my brother over a piece of land that neither of us is going to take with us.
let go, clinging
fish, greed, trap
Write a doha about a fish who sees something tasty and swims straight to it, not knowing there is a hidden hook within, a picture of how the pleasures of the world tempt us to our own undoing.
doha about a fish that bites what looks like food
I clicked on an ad promising easy money, put in my savings, and lost the lot, and my father said I swallowed it like a fish.
The fish rushes after the glitter and swallows its own end.
deceptive world
Compose a doha for someone who is tired of chasing success and wealth and who wants to remember that the whole show of the world is temporary, so the heart can stop clinging.
After watching my father lose his business to a fraud, I sat down with him and neither of us could say what we had really lost.
The world is a bright and fleeting fair, and the wise leave it as lightly as they came.
doha on worldly things not being real
I stayed up till 3 AM scrolling a screen glowing like a lamp, and thought, I'm exactly like a moth; I know it's bad and still can't leave.
The moth knows not the lamp's cruelty, only its call, and the call is enough to ruin him.

Write a doha about the moth that keeps circling the lamp, taking its glow for something worth having, not knowing the beautiful brightness is the very thing that destroys him, like our greed for the world.
doha: moth circling lamp but its about being fooled by the world
moth, lamp, deception
My mother used to bring me to the Saturday market and we would watch people spend and haggle all day for things they'd forget by Monday.

Compose a doha about a crowded market full of colourful things that people buy and fight over, each convinced it will make them happy, and all of it being just a passing show that ends when the day does.
doha pls: busy market, everyone chasing stuff
The market sings with colour and coin, and all that is bought there is lent.
market, vain chasing
doha on how the world tricks us into thinking things will last
Please write a doha about someone who realises late in life that the praise, property and power he spent decades gathering were never his and that he mistook a passing show for reality.
false permanence
I retired last month, and after all those years chasing promotions I feel like I woke up in someone else's life.
He who wakes from the fair finds his hands full of nothing.
Flutter, small moth, flutter; the glitter you love was built to burn you.
doha with a moth for greed pls

Write a doha about a moth who flies toward a glittering thing it cannot resist, even though it is certain to be hurt, like a person who keeps running after the world's pleasures knowing they bring pain.
My friend keeps going back to a gambling app, knowing he'll lose every time, and says he can't stay away, like a moth.
moth, desire, ruin
My neighbour, a potter, built a big house from his clay work and spends every night worrying about it, though the house isn't even finished.
Compose a doha about a potter who takes such pride in the clay vessels he makes, thinking they are everything, and does not see that they are only clay that will be broken, as all things in life are.
doha about a potter being too attached to his clay stuff
The potter loves his vessels as if they were forever, and clay remembers it was dust.
potter, clay, attachment
doha about prayer beads and being stuck on worldly stuff
prayer beads, attachment
My neighbour does his prayer beads every dawn then rushes to check the share prices on his phone before he's even done.

Write a doha about a worshipper who turns his prayer beads for hours, yet whose heart is tangled in money and possessions, showing that outer practice does not release the one who still clings inside.
Many are the beads, and many more the ties that bind the heart to the world.
market, vanishing wealth
Write a doha about a merchant in the busy market who counts his coins all day and believes he is rich, though everything he holds is borrowed and will be gone before he understands it.
doha about the market and getting rich, but it's all fake
My father ran a stall in the old market for thirty years, and when it closed he found he'd been holding on to nothing.
In the marketplace the buyer and seller both are fooled, and the prices are written on air.
write a doha on why attachment is pointless
I kept every gift my ex ever gave me for two years, and when I finally threw them out, I felt lighter than I had in ages.
attachment, loss, letting go
Lost is what was never held, and what seemed mine was only passing through.
I want a doha for someone who is grieving the loss of things they were attached to, a reminder that the world gives and takes in turn, and that nothing we cling to was ever truly ours.
Compose a doha about a man who lives all his life at the bottom of a well, proud of the small world around him and its little treasures, unaware of the wide truth waiting above.
well, narrow world
I never traveled in my life, and at fifty-five my daughter dragged me on a trip and I saw how small my corner had been, like a well.
At the bottom of the well he rules his little kingdom, and calls the circle of sky above his own.
doha: guy in a well thinks its the whole world
My brother is in debt for a wedding he thought would make everyone respect him, and the respect has not come.
He built his joy on the opinion of others, and woke to find it only an echo.
doha on how appearances and status are meaningless
status, pretence

Please write a doha about how society teaches us to want titles, wealth and a good name, though these are only shadows of happiness, and about how the wise person stays unmoved by their rise and fall.
The mango tree in our yard fruited every summer and I thought it would always be there, but last year a storm took it in an hour.
tree, lost shade
pls doha about a tree and how we shouldn't get attached to it
Under the tree's green shade the traveller forgets that the road continues.
Write a doha about a traveler who rests under a tree, takes the shade as his own, and starts to build his hopes there, forgetting he has to leave soon, like all of us in this temporary world.
well, deceptive depth
doha about a well where people keep drawing water but are never satisfied

Write a doha about a well that seems deep and full of promise, drawing people with its depth, though every time they lower their bucket for water they pull up only thirst, showing how the world deceives its seekers.
Deep is the well the world has dug for thirst, and none has drunk his fill.
I've been chasing the next big thing for years, always sure it would satisfy me, but every time I get there it's like a well that never fills.
